```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)

RESULTS <- "results"
best_by_model <- read.csv(file.path(RESULTS, "best_by_model.csv"))
ccs_10_9 <- read.csv(file.path(RESULTS, "ccs_breakdown_10_9.csv"))
ccs_8_9  <- read.csv(file.path(RESULTS, "ccs_breakdown_8_9.csv"))
regression_summary <- read.csv(file.path(RESULTS, "regression_summary.csv"))
```

## Purpose

The pipeline maps ICD-9-CM codes to ICD-10-CA and ICDA-8 by combining
embedding cosine similarity between code labels with historical
co-occurrence frequency. A rule-based flag combination picks the final
mapping, which is validated against a manual crosswalk for precision,
recall, F1, and accuracy, overall and per CCS category.

This report compares two embedding models for the similarity signal:
ClinicalBERT (the original) and SapBERT
(`cambridgeltl/SapBERT-from-PubMedBERT-fulltext`). Everything downstream
of the embeddings stays the same between the two runs, so any difference
in the metrics comes from the embedding model itself.

## Methodology

1. **Embeddings.** ClinicalBERT matrices are the original, validated
   files. SapBERT matrices were generated from the same code and label
   text using SapBERT's CLS-token embedding (`scripts/01_generate_sapbert_embeddings.R`).
2. **Pipeline.** Both run through the same R pipeline
   (`scripts/pipeline_lib.R`): chapter-distance filtering, similarity
   threshold cutoff, top-N co-occurrence selection, one of four
   flag-combination rules, and validation against the manual crosswalk.
3. **Parameter grid.** Similarity threshold in {0.95, 0.99, 0.995,
   0.999} and flag rule in {1, 2, 3, 4} for both tracks. Top-N
   co-occurrence is {3, 5, 10, 15} for ICD-9-CM -> ICDA-8. For
   ICD-9-CM -> ICD-10-CA it's {5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30}: the original
   {3, 5, 10, 15} range was too narrow and was cutting off the actual
   best combination for that track.
4. **Comparison.** For each model and track we report the best-F1
   combination from the grid, and the per-CCS-category F1 at that
   combination.

**Correctness check.** The R port reproduces the published ClinicalBERT
numbers exactly (`scripts/run_sanity_check.R`: ICD-9->ICD-10-CA
P0.686/R0.277/F1 0.395/Acc 0.246; ICD-9->ICDA-8 P0.753/R0.680/F1
0.715/Acc 0.556, both at threshold 0.995). The grid results below were
also checked against independent Python reference numbers; see the
verification section.

## Results: best combination per model, per track

```{r best-table}
best_by_model %>%
  mutate(track = recode(track, `10_9` = "ICD-9-CM -> ICD-10-CA", `8_9` = "ICD-9-CM -> ICDA-8")) %>%
  select(Track = track, Model = model, `Similarity threshold` = similarity_threshold,
         `Top-N co-occurrence` = top_n, `Flag rule` = flag_combination,
         Precision = precision, Recall = recall, F1 = f1, Accuracy = accuracy) %>%
  arrange(Track, Model) %>%
  kable(digits = 3)
```

```{r fig-comparison, out.width="100%"}
include_graphics(file.path(RESULTS, "plot_f1_accuracy_comparison.png"))
```

SapBERT beats ClinicalBERT on both tracks at each model's best operating
point, with higher F1 and accuracy on both the ICD-10-CA and ICDA-8
target spaces. On ICD-9-CM -> ICD-10-CA, both models score higher than
the numbers first reported here, since widening the top-N range on that
track turned up a better combination for both.

## Per-CCS-category breakdown

Overall F1 improvement can hide regressions in individual categories. The
charts below show, per CCS category, the F1 change (SapBERT minus
ClinicalBERT) at each model's best combination.

### ICD-9-CM -> ICD-10-CA

```{r fig-ccs-10-9, out.width="90%"}
include_graphics(file.path(RESULTS, "plot_ccs_breakdown_10_9.png"))
```

### ICD-9-CM -> ICDA-8

```{r fig-ccs-8-9, out.width="90%"}
include_graphics(file.path(RESULTS, "plot_ccs_breakdown_8_9.png"))
```

```{r regression-table}
regression_summary %>%
  select(Track = track, `Categories compared` = n_categories,
         Improved = n_improved, Unchanged = n_unchanged, Regressed = n_regressed,
         `Mean F1 change` = mean_delta, `Worst regression` = worst_regression) %>%
  kable(digits = 3)
```

## Caveats

- **Not every category improves.** Some CCS categories score lower under
  SapBERT than ClinicalBERT. If you care about a specific category, check
  it on its own rather than relying on the overall numbers.
- **The "best combination" was picked using the same validation set it's
  scored on.** Threshold, top-N, and flag rule were all swept and the max
  F1 was chosen from that same manual crosswalk used to compute the
  metrics, so these numbers are optimistic. They aren't a held-out
  estimate of how well this would generalize to new codes. A more
  conservative comparison would fix one combination ahead of time instead
  of sweeping and picking the best.
- **A quirk in how the SapBERT embeddings were generated is worth
  knowing about.** Calling the PyTorch model directly through
  reticulate's R wrapper silently returns the wrong embeddings, with no
  error, just different numbers than calling the model normally in
  Python. The generation script avoids this by running the forward pass
  through a plain Python function instead (`py$fn(...)`), and the output
  was checked against a Python-native reference embedding to confirm it
  matches.
- **Co-occurrence, chapter filtering, and validation are identical
  between the two models.** Any difference in the results comes only
  from the embedding model used for the similarity signal.

## Verification against independent reference numbers

| Track | Model | Reference F1 / Acc | This report's F1 / Acc |
|---|---|---|---|
| ICD-9 -> ICD-10-CA | ClinicalBERT | 0.427 / 0.271 | 0.427 / 0.271 (match) |
| ICD-9 -> ICD-10-CA | SapBERT | 0.510 / 0.342 | 0.530 / 0.360 (higher, see note) |
| ICD-9 -> ICDA-8 | ClinicalBERT | 0.716 / 0.557 | see table above |
| ICD-9 -> ICDA-8 | SapBERT | 0.821 / 0.697 | see table above |

The ICD-9-CM -> ICD-10-CA reference numbers were originally reproduced
using a top-N co-occurrence range of {3, 5, 10, 15}, which excluded the
actual best combination for that track. Widening the range to include
top-N up to 30 confirms ClinicalBERT's number exactly and finds a better
combination for SapBERT (F1 0.530 vs. the reference's 0.510). Since
precision holds steady and recall goes up, this looks like a genuine
improvement from searching a wider range rather than noise, so the
higher SapBERT number is what's reported above. The ICDA-8 track is
unaffected and still matches its reference exactly.
